en: Udāna 2.6 Gabbhinīsutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time a certain wanderer had a young wife who was pregnant and about to give birth.
Then that female wanderer said this to the wanderer:
“Go, brahmin, bring some oil for when I have given birth.
When this was said, that wanderer said to that female wanderer:
“But from where, lady, shall I bring the oil?”
A second time, that female wanderer said this to that male wanderer:
"Go, brahmin, fetch some oil for when I have given birth.
A second time, that male wanderer said this to that female wanderer:
“But from where, lady, shall I bring oil?
For a third time, that female wanderer said this to the male wanderer:
“Go, brahmin, and bring oil, which will be for me when I have given birth.”
Now at that time, in the storehouse of King Pasenadi of Kosala, ghee or oil was being given to any ascetic or brahmin who wished to drink as much as they required, but not to take away.
Then it occurred to that wanderer:
"In the storehouse of King Pasenadi of Kosala, ghee or oil is being given to any ascetic or brahmin who wishes to drink as much as they require, but not to take away."
"What if I were to go to the storehouse of King Pasenadi of Kosala, drink as much oil as I need, return home, and having vomited it up, give it to her for the child she will bear?
Then that wanderer went to the storehouse of King Pasenadi of Kosala, drank as much oil as he needed, and returned home; yet he was unable to either move it upward or downward.
Afflicted by painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations, he writhed and rolled about.
Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
There he saw that wanderer afflicted by painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations, writhing and rolling about.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Happy indeed are those who possess nothing,
for people who have attained knowledge are truly without possessions.
Behold one who possesses something being tormented!”
"A person whose mind is bound to another person.
The sixth.
